headline: Local Man Files Supreme Court Petition To Prosecute His Own Subconscious For Deleting Memories Of Where He Kept His Car Keys
body:
Frustrated by the persistent disappearance of his belongings, local accountant Ramesh Iyer has formally petitioned the Supreme Court to initiate a Special Investigation Team (SIT) inquiry into his own brain for what he describes as 'unauthorized and suspicious data deletion' of his car keys’ location.

Iyer, who stood for hours in his parking lot this morning, claims his subconscious has been acting as an 'unaccountable constitutional authority' by systematically erasing memories of where he last placed his essential items. “I am not asking for much, just a transparent, judicial oversight into why my own internal electoral college decided to strike my keys from the master registry of things I recall,” said Iyer, who was forced to take a rickshaw to work despite having a perfectly functional sedan.

Legal experts are divided on whether the Supreme Court has the jurisdiction to investigate the internal workings of a private individual’s hippocampus. “While we respect the right to petition for a fair memory-recall process, the judiciary is generally reluctant to subpoena a citizen’s frontal lobe, as it lacks a physical office where the SIT can serve the summons,” noted senior constitutional lawyer Vikram Batra.

As of press time, Iyer’s subconscious was unavailable for comment, though it did reportedly assist him in remembering the lyrics to a random 90s commercial jingle while he was attempting to find his spare set of house keys.
caption: Supreme Court now expected to handle every lost item, starting with the keys you left in your pocket yesterday. Don't worry, the SIT is already on its way. (satire) #SupremeCourt #MemoryLoss #JudicialReform #JusticeForKeys
